chapter: New Orleans trombone style and composing
title: Father bowing the bass and insisting on lessons first
summary: His father bowed the bass and insisted on lessons before playing popular tunes; Joseph teaches his own son valve and slide, and only took up valve trombone recently.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Well no, now I see, now I'm glad you see that. That's the honest way my dad could play. With the bow? With the bow.
That's what I hear. The old timers always said they played the bow a lot. You don't see that
and hear it anymore now. No, he used to bow. But I just fool around with it, you know. Because I remember I'd be fooling around with it. He used to say, oh, quit picking that thing man.
Boy, quit picking. Is he a pretty strict musician? Did he help you on things or? Well, some of those old timers they tell you. I'll tell you one thing about it though Bill.

I'm glad he done it. Like if you know like a kid he'd be trying to blow something on his own like a poplar tune or something like that. But when I picked up my horn, he wanted me to start my lesson off first. Then after I remember my lesson off a while, well he didn't care what I do after that. Used to see that when I got in me so that's what I always did too. And he didn't know how to read the music, but he knew what was supposed to happen, you know.

So that is the same thing, what I'm doing with my kid. See, I know it's time coming that you have to know both of the horns, the valve and the slide. So I had him to start off on the valve first. Now he practiced, after Auburn he practiced a while with the slide then and the valve. Practiced both of them.
Well, I guess you never, when you were young you didn't use the valve, huh?
Oh no, no. I just got the valve, well after, oh about five or six years ago.
